task.title: Repair provider-report probe call signature without changing fleet policy

scope.owned_layer: Supervisor entrypoint module identity, focused provider-report config-bearing tick regression coverage, and task-scoped review evidence.
scope.not_changing: Provider probe projection semantics, failure hysteresis, auth or quota state, account grouping, fleet limits, task scheduling or reviewer policy, credentials, live runtime files, or supervisor processes.

incident.observed_error: TypeError: apply_provider_probe_to_report() got an unexpected keyword argument 'config'
incident.root_cause: The daemon executes the pinned supervisor file as __main__, while provider_permissions imports apply_provider_probe_to_report lazily from the module name supervisor. A second supervisor module can therefore resolve from another checkout in the same process. The confirmed status-root source shape still has the legacy three-argument function, while the pinned runtime caller passes config=.
incident.reproduction: The focused regression installs a legacy three-argument supervisor module, confirms the config-bearing refreshed report raises the observed TypeError before binding, binds the running __main__ implementation, and then proves probe_provider_reports completes through load_provider_report_tick.

call_signature_inventory.location: provider_capabilities lazy import and live-probe projection
call_signature_inventory.shape: from supervisor import apply_provider_probe_to_report; apply_provider_probe_to_report(report, pkey, auth_probe, config=config)

repair.mechanism: When and only when supervisor.py is the running __main__ module, bind sys.modules['supervisor'] to that same module before provider_permissions is imported.
repair.normal_import_behavior: Importing supervisor normally leaves sys.modules unchanged because __name__ is supervisor rather than __main__.
repair.compatibility_effect: The lazy provider_permissions import always resolves the function implemented by the running supervisor runtime, so its caller and signature cannot come from different checkouts.
repair.policy_effect: None. The function body and all provider, hysteresis, auth, quota, scheduling, and persistence decisions are unchanged.

pinned_shape_and_typeerror_reproduced.proof: The test asserts the legacy module raises the exact unexpected-config TypeError before binding.

config_bearing_tick_repaired.proof: After binding, probe_provider_reports projects a failed live probe with config and updates the report through load_provider_report_tick without TypeError.

call_sites_identified.proof: The source and pinned runtime each contain one compatible definition and three production calls; every production caller remains config-compatible.

provider_semantics_preserved.proof: Focused provider recovery suites and the full supervisor suite pass without changing apply_provider_probe_to_report or scheduler logic.

source_only_boundary.proof: The task diff is limited to supervisor source, its test, and this evidence manifest; no live runtime, task state, credential, configuration, or process mutation was performed.
